verses.1: I am willing to gather my people together. Let them listen to my words. Let them hear what I say.
verses.2: She opened her mouth and spoke these mysteries before me.
verses.3: We have heard and known about this; our ancestors also told us about it.
verses.4: We shall not be deceived by their appearances in this world. For in the future, we will know about the praises of Jehovah, His miracles, and all the things He has done.
verses.5: And he established a law in Jacob, and Torah was given to Israel. This law commanded our ancestors to teach it to their children.
verses.6: So that their descendants will know, when they are born, that they have lived and fulfilled their duties to their children.
verses.7: And they shall serve God with all their heart, and they shall not forget the sins of God and His commandments.
verses.8: And they shall not be like those who are cruel and harsh, who are not prepared to listen to others’ opinions. Nor shall they believe in the Lord of Spirits.
verses.9: In the children of Ephraim, those who wept over the loss of their loved ones, they were comforted on that day of sorrow.
verses.10: They did not keep God’s covenant and His laws as they should have.
verses.11: And they forgot their wives and children, whom they had brought into the world.
verses.12: Against their fathers, he made a field in the land of Egypt. It was a field for grazing sheep.
verses.13: He divided the sea, and he brought them across. He made the waters stand still, just like a bed.
verses.14: And it was dark in the sky during the day, and all night long, it was lit by fire.
verses.15: It destroyed the insects in the desert, and it covered many of them with mud.
verses.16: And they came out of the rocks, and they went down along the rivers of water.
verses.17: And they continued to sin against Him, even in the wilderness.
verses.18: And they went to him in their hearts, asking for food for their souls.
verses.19: And they spoke to God, saying, “May one person be able to make a altar in the wilderness.”
verses.20: And there were also mountains that were destroyed; rivers and streams were flooded. Even bread could not be stored, as there was no place left for it in the land.
verses.21: So, when Jehovah heard this, he sent fire upon Jacob. And also, smoke rose up over Israel.
verses.22: For they did not believe in God, and they did not trust in His salvation.
verses.23: And he commanded that the gates of heaven be opened.
verses.24: And he provided them with food to eat. He also gave them fish from the heavens.
verses.25: Manor lords ate bread. One of them sent them food to eat.
verses.26: He would travel through the heavens and govern with his own will.
verses.27: And he spread over them a layer of water, like clouds of water.
verses.28: And he lay down near his tent, around his dwelling place.
verses.29: And they ate and rejoiced greatly; their joy came upon them.
verses.30: They didn’t stop eating from their mouths because of their anger.
verses.31: And God descended upon them, and he killed them in their midst. And He destroyed the cities of Israel.
verses.32: In all this, they still sinned and did not believe in His miracles.
verses.33: And their days and years were filled with darkness.
verses.34: If they are killed, and they are demanded as prisoners, and they return and are captured…
verses.35: And they remembered that God created them, and that He is their Creator.
verses.36: And they praised him with their lips and in their words.
verses.37: And their hearts were not willing to go with him, and they did not trust his covenant.
verses.38: And he will be merciful and not destroy those who are in distress. He will also restore many to their rightful place, and he will not raise up any who are in trouble.
verses.39: And he remembered that those who were alive still had spirits that moved around, and they would never return.
verses.40: How many days will they spend in the desert; how much sorrow will they endure there.
verses.41: And they returned and sought him. And the Holy One of Israel was found.
verses.42: They did not remember their hands on the day they were rescued from my hands.
verses.43: In Egypt, he placed his statues and idols in the fields of worship.
verses.44: And their eyes became bloodshot, and their tears turned into blood.
verses.45: He will send them away at dusk, and they will be eaten by the birds.
verses.46: And He gave to Hesil Yevulam and Igiyam the power to rule over them.
verses.47: Their arms will be broken, and their legs will be tied up in the prison.
verses.48: And he sealed the barracks in their cities and their properties for the descendants of Rishaf.
verses.49: He will send them away, along with anger, sorrow, and suffering, from the hands of those who do evil.
verses.50: May their path be made straight, so that their souls and lives may not be destroyed by death. May they live according to the words of the Torah.
verses.51: And in all the cemeteries of Egypt, at first, there were graves in the hot places.
verses.52: And he led his people like a flock of sheep, and he guided them through the wilderness.
verses.53: And they were at ease and not afraid, and their enemies were covered by the sea.
verses.54: And he brought them to the holy land of Mount Zeh. There, his right hand was acquired.
verses.55: And he drove them away from their lands. He scattered them across the territory of the valley. They settled in their tents, as did the Israelites.
verses.56: And they tried to defy and mock God and His miracles. They did not keep them in mind.
verses.57: And they became like stones, because of their suffering. They became like broken pieces of pottery.
verses.58: And they provoked him with their words and their actions.
verses.59: God heard this, and His anger was greatly stirred in Israel.
verses.60: And he went from Shilo’s tent to the tent of the man.
verses.61: And he gave his wife Uz and her beauty to the king.
verses.62: And he sealed his people and their land.
verses.63: In their openings, there was fire; in their endings, there was no sound.
verses.64: Their priests fell in the battle, and their prophets were not mourned.
verses.65: And he stretched out his hand as if it were a weapon, like a mighty ruler who can do anything he wants.
verses.66: And his enemies were subjected to eternal shame and disgrace.
verses.67: And he lay down in Joseph’s tent, and in Ephraim’s camp, without choosing a place.
verses.68: And he chose the tribe of Judah to be located on Mount Zion, which he loved.
verses.69: And he created them like mountains from his holy place, as if they were land established for eternity.
verses.70: And David chose his servant, and took him from the flocks of the sheep.
verses.71: After his rise, he brought it down upon Jacob’s people and upon Israel’s land.
verses.72: And his heart was filled with sorrow, and his hands trembled.
